title: OTLP Smart Gateway: tenant-aware handoff + sampled-trace propagation
creator: Aisha Malik
description:
Problem statement:
Redwood routing for traces currently assumes a single best-effort exporter path. For high-volume tenants and transient backend outages (Tempo or Jaeger), we need a gateway that preserves sampling decisions, applies per-tenant routing/priority, and provides a durable, bounded handoff buffer with spill-to-blob fallback for audit and replay. Without this, customers see trace loss or severe tail latency during exporter backpressure.

Goal:
Implement an OTLP Smart Gateway that: 1) decodes and preserves sampled-trace flags and parent/trace IDs, 2) applies per-tenant routing policy (can dual-write to Tempo + Jaeger or fanout to third-party vendor), 3) supports graceful backpressure with an in-memory TTL buffer + local disk ring buffer + optional S3 spill-to-archive for retention and replay, 4) signs/rotates per-tenant credentials for downstream exporters, and 5) emits observability metrics and tracing for the gateway itself so we can debug failures and latency.

Success criteria / acceptance tests (high level):
- End-to-end tracing: a synthetic trace that traverses service -> gateway -> exporter(s) must preserve traceID/spanIDs and sampled flag in all destinations in 98th percentile.
- Loss tolerance: under an artificial tempo outage the gateway must spill to disk and S3 without dropping more than 1% of spans for tenants with retention-policy enabled.
- Latency SLO: gateway adds <5ms p50 and <25ms p99 additional latency when all exporters healthy; under backpressure metrics should show controlled shed/buffer behavior instead of unbounded latency.
- Policy correctness: per-tenant routing rules (routeA->tempo, routeB->jaeger+vendor) are respected across restarts and key rotations.
- Security: credential rotation occurs without request drops; audit logs contain exporter handoff records for at least 7 days for regulated tenants.

Design notes / trade-offs considered:
- Buffering hierarchy: in-memory queue (fast, small) -> local ring buffer (durable, bounded) -> S3 spill (durable, high-latency). This reduces memory pressure while preserving replayability at cost of increased complexity and S3 egress.
- Dual write semantics: implement at-least-once delivery to reduce complexity. To control downstream duplication we will mark synthetic envelope metadata (gateway-id + sequence) so consumers can deduplicate if desired. Implementing strict exactly-once across heterogeneous exporters is infeasible and would require coordinator state and distributed consensus.
- Sampling propagation: require the gateway to honor incoming TraceFlags.sampled and not force-resample except for tenants with configured override policies. This maintains end-to-end fidelity for customer-specified sampling.
- Credentials: use per-tenant short-lived tokens signed by gateway KMS. A small credential rotation service (library) will be part of the gateway; rotation scheme will be pluggable for Dedicated/Private modes.

Implementation plan (milestones):
1) Spike (week 1): prototype local ring buffer and synthetic dual-write to a Tempo mock. Deliver: spike report + perf numbers.
2) Core gateway (weeks 2-4): OTLP ingestion, tenant extraction, routing rules engine, in-memory queue + local ring buffer, exporter adapters for Tempo and Jaeger.
3) Resilience features (weeks 5-6): S3 spill-to-archive, replay API for rehydration, credential rotation integration.
4) Observability + tests (weeks 6-7): internal gateway metrics, tracing, chaos tests, long-run soak tests.
5) Rollout (week 8): gradual canary in staging -> prod with per-tenant toggles and fallback to legacy path.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for routing engine and exporter shim with mocked OTLP payloads.
- Integration tests: end-to-end with tempo/jaeger docker containers in CI.
- Fault injection: simulate exporter 5xxs/latency and assert buffering/spill behavior.
- Durability test: restart gateway mid-spill and assert replay completes.
- Load test: 100K spans/sec synthetic traffic with variable span sizes to validate buffer sizing and p99 latencies.

Rollout plan and observability:
- Feature flag. Start with internal tenants only. Monitor gateway.metrics.{ingest_latency,p99,p50,export_failures,buffer_usage,spill_events} and Redwood Console dashboards for errors and tail latency. Use automatic rollback if exporter_fail_rate > 0.5% over 5 minutes for tiered customers.

Open decisions / unknowns:
- Deduplication downstream: whether to provide a consumer-side dedupe helper lib or rely on vendors. Currently favor consumer dedupe metadata.
- S3 lifecycle: recommended policy (30/90/365) needs compliance input for regulated tenants.
- Compression: index vs non-indexed blobs when spilling to S3 (trade-off between faster replay vs smaller storage).

acceptance_criteria: TraceIDs and sampled flag preserved across dual-write destinations in e2e tests
Buffer spill-to-disk and S3 demonstrated in chaos test with <1% span loss for configured tenants
Gateway adds <5ms p50 and <25ms p99 latency when exporters healthy
Per-tenant routing rules enforced across restarts
Credential rotation performed without request drops and audit logs retained
